A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TUNER and provide readable main texts and complete supplements. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures and tables can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-reconstruction experiments, signal and gradient PSNR results, initialization and bounding ablations, and baseline comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds regularization and depth ablations plus quantitative DIV2K comparisons.

M1.justification: Frequency sampling, Gaussian hidden-weight initialization, fixed clipping, learnable tanh bounds and the L1 regularizer remain unchanged. Replacing c_L with c_* clarifies the already stated column-specific initialization bound. The deeper-network experiments apply existing components rather than introduce a new method.

E1.justification: The supplement adds DIV2K to the retained Kodak coverage, including a BANF comparison using images rescaled to 256×256 and evaluated at 512×512. This extends dataset and resolution coverage within the existing image-reconstruction domain.

E2.justification: FINER, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated comparator alongside FFM in supplementary Table 3. SIREN, BACON, BANF and FFM were already evaluated in v2; their existing comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Added BANF experiments substantially extend evaluation design through matched training time, fresh TUNER training at each level of detail, evaluation across resolutions, and an explicit out-of-band error metric. Separate studies introduce two-hidden-layer configurations and 1000/5000-epoch FFM/FINER comparisons. The existing Kodak protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds an on/off ablation of the existing regularizer. Supplementary Section 2.3 extends the capacity analysis to two hidden layers, comparing uniform initialization, TUNER initialization alone and full TUNER. Existing frequency-sampling and bounding ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v3 removes the Section 5.1 summary giving average standard deviations of 1.9 dB for signal and 3.1 dB for gradients alongside Table 1. Other standard-deviation reporting remains. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, but substantial supplementary results are added. At bands 64/256, new TUNER versus BANF PSNR values are 26.31/22.96 and 32.65/29.59 dB. Additional entries cover spectral error, FINER/FFM comparisons, deeper networks and regularization. Section 5.1 also newly supplies the absolute initialization scores, 36.2 versus 32.2 dB. These are added results, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 removes the erroneous equality preceding supplementary Theorem 2, corrects the column/row description in Theorem 3's proof, and adds the recursion convention for i=2. The principal theorems and derivations remain. Supplementary Section 2.4 also introduces the mathematical definition of ErrorFFT.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims about amplitude-phase expansion, initialization, spectral control and stable training. The three-layer terminology clarifies the previously specified architecture; theoretical generalization to deeper networks already appeared in v2's supplement.

C2.justification: The supplement adds interpretations concerning applicability to deeper networks, BANF performance without residual-based TUNER training, and FFM/FINER tradeoffs between gradient smoothness and detail reconstruction. The main limitations concerning image-focused experiments and further investigation of deep networks remain.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly identifies Sobel filtering as the ground-truth gradient reference, without establishing a change to earlier evaluations. Added experiments disclose layer sizes, bounds, training steps, FINER initialization, TUNER's period and a 5×10^-4 learning rate. No new code-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The discussion of Yüce et al. expands to distinguish bias handling and deep-network generalization, and the DIV2K dataset paper is newly cited. FINER, FRESH and other references with completed bibliographic details were already present in v2.

P1.justification: v3 refines terminology, rewrites several supplementary explanations, shortens the conclusion, completes bibliographic entries and adds acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and research narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The supplement adds three tables and two comparison figures. Existing figures are resized or relocated, several captions clarify gradient displays, and main Table 1 gains a high-frequency-percentage heading. The established visual organization is largely retained.

improvement.justification: The regularizer ablation, quantitative spectral-leakage evaluation and limited deeper-network study strengthen support for existing claims. The Sobel disclosure and mathematical corrections improve reproducibility and precision. These gains outweigh limited reporting regressions: the removed variability summary and the new 'at least 3 dB' BANF assertion, although supplementary Figure 8 includes a 31.3 versus 28.9 dB example, only 2.4 dB apart.
